hypothesis: Bulk 72 h growth reflects statistical detectability of population expansion rather than the first cell-cycle event.
public_support: 2025 Pv11-00443-Or47a cell counts are stable through 48 h and first significantly different from 1 h baseline at 72 h, but direct S-phase/mitosis timing was not measured.
key_prediction: Direct cell-cycle entry can precede significant bulk count increase.
decisive_test: Dense 0-96 h EdU/BrdU or equivalent S-phase plus mitotic/cell-cycle-state measurements in the same population.
kill_rule: If validated direct cell-cycle readouts remain absent until the same ~72 h boundary, assay-threshold-only explanation is weakened.

hypothesis: Unresolved DNA damage or a repair/checkpoint state delays cell-cycle entry.
public_support: Repair programs are active during rehydration, but no matched perturbation currently links repair-state completion to first S-phase timing in Polypedilum/Pv11.
key_prediction: Increasing unresolved relevant damage or impairing a relevant repair/checkpoint component shifts first S-phase/mitosis later; rescue shifts it back.
decisive_test: Matched damage-state + cell-cycle time course with orthogonal perturbation and rescue in the same tissue/cell system.
kill_rule: If first cell-cycle entry timing is unchanged despite a validated change in unresolved damage/repair state, reject or sharply weaken this gate for that system.

hypothesis: Different DNA-damage classes recover on different clocks and no single scalar 'DNA repair completion' exists.
public_support: 2023 oxidative-damage assays report repair within a few hours, whereas 2010 fat-body alkaline comet fragmentation returns to baseline by ~96 h with little recovery in first 24 h.
key_prediction: Early recovery/cell-cycle events may coexist with unresolved lesion classes that are not rate-limiting for that event.
decisive_test: Measure at least two lesion classes in the same tissue/population alongside cell-cycle entry.
kill_rule: If validated independent lesion assays collapse to one common recovery trajectory under matched conditions, multiplex model is weakened.

hypothesis: Delayed bulk expansion is partly determined by founder survival and recovery lag rather than a dedicated cell-cycle checkpoint.
public_support: 2018 Hsf knockdown reduced post-rehydration survival ~5-fold but did not significantly alter proliferation rate after excluding day 1 (reported P=0.3).
key_prediction: Manipulations that change survival can change absolute population curves without changing the growth rate of survivors.
decisive_test: Normalize post-rehydration growth to viable founder number and independently measure first cell-cycle entry.
kill_rule: If founder-normalized growth delay remains tightly coupled to repair state and shifts with repair perturbation, survival-bottleneck-only explanation is insufficient.

hypothesis: Cells require staged functional/proteostatic/metabolic rebuilding before robust population expansion, independently of complete DNA-repair status.
public_support: 2025 Pv11 functional assays show some activity at ~1 h and de-novo-protein-dependent receptor response recovery from ~12-24 h, before significant bulk growth at 72 h.
key_prediction: Recovery markers for translation/metabolic competence precede bulk proliferation and may better predict first cell-cycle entry than a global repair endpoint.
decisive_test: Matched time course of translation/metabolic recovery, damage-state measures, and direct cell-cycle entry.
kill_rule: If cell-cycle entry tracks only damage/checkpoint state after controlling for metabolic/proteostatic recovery, this explanation is weakened.

hypothesis: Different tissues or cell states restart cell cycling on different schedules after rehydration.
public_support: Public fat-body DNA-repair measurements are tissue-specific; whole-larva behavioral recovery is organism-level; Pv11 is an embryonic cell line, so current evidence roots are not interchangeable.
key_prediction: Tissue-resolved cell-cycle entry distributions will be broad or multimodal rather than represented by one organism-wide onset time.
decisive_test: Tissue-resolved 0-96 h S-phase/mitosis measurements with matched lesion-state readouts.
kill_rule: If all validated tissues show the same narrow cell-cycle onset under matched conditions, heterogeneity explanation is weakened.
